name: Singapore Do Not Call (DNC) Registry
summary: Stop unsolicited telemarketing calls, SMS and messaging-app marketing (including WhatsApp) to your Singapore numbers. Free and does not expire.
processingTime: Protection starts 21 calendar days after registration
requirements: A Singapore phone number you control
Ability to receive an SMS or phone call on that number if using SMS or phone registration
steps: Go to dnc.gov.sg, the Personal Data Protection Commission's official DNC Registry site, and choose Register.
Enter your Singapore mobile, home or office number and choose which types of messages to block: voice calls, text messages (SMS, MMS, WhatsApp and similar apps) or fax.

Complete the verification step. Alternatively, SMS "DNC" to 78771 from the number you want to register (standard SMS charges apply), or call the toll-free line 1800 248 0771 from that number. Do not use a phone that blocks caller ID for the call option.
Wait 21 calendar days. After that, organisations must not send you telemarketing messages on the registered number unless you gave clear consent or have an ongoing relationship with them.
If you still receive telemarketing after 21 days, file a complaint through the DNC Registry website.
relistingWarning: Registration is free and does not expire, but it only covers the numbers you register (register every number you own). It does not remove your data from broker or people-search databases and does not stop marketing from organisations you gave consent to. Withdraw consent with those senders directly.

name: Hong Kong Do-not-call Registers (OFCA)
summary: Register your Hong Kong numbers on the statutory Do-not-call Registers to block commercial pre-recorded calls, SMS and fax messages from all senders.
processingTime: Protection starts on the 10th working day after registration
requirements: A Hong Kong telephone or mobile number you control
steps: Decide which registers you need. Hong Kong operates three under the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance (Cap. 593): pre-recorded telephone messages, short messages (SMS/MMS) and fax messages.
Register through the Office of the Communications Authority (OFCA) at dnc.gov.hk, or call the registration hotline 1835 000 from the number you want to register.
Register each number separately, and each register separately.
Note that protection begins on the 10th working day after registration. You can check your registration date at dnc.gov.hk.

To stop marketing you consented to, or messages that are not covered, use the unsubscribe facility that every commercial message must contain, or make an opt-out request under the PDPO (see our Hong Kong direct marketing opt-out guide).
relistingWarning: The registers only cover the specific numbers and message types you register. They do not cover person-to-person live calls, and they do not remove your details from marketing lists or people-search sites. You can be contacted by senders you have an existing relationship with.

name: Hong Kong Direct Marketing Opt-out (PDPO s35G)
summary: Under Hong Kong's Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, you can tell any company to stop using your personal data for direct marketing, and to stop passing it to third parties, free of charge.
processingTime: Company must comply without charge once you ask; there is no fixed public processing window, so follow up in writing
requirements: The name of the company sending marketing
Your name and the contact details they hold (phone, email, address)
steps: Identify the company using your data (check the sender of the call, SMS or email, or the privacy notice you received).

Send a written request (email or letter) to the company's data protection or privacy officer stating: you are exercising your right under section 35G of the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance to stop your personal data being used in direct marketing, and, if applicable, section 35L to stop it being provided to others for their direct marketing.
Ask them to notify any third party they have already given your data to so those parties stop using it too.
Keep a dated copy of your request and their reply.
If the company ignores you or keeps marketing, you can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD), which has taken enforcement action over ignored opt-out requests.
relistingWarning: This is a request per company, not a central list, and each company must be contacted separately. Your data may re-enter marketing lists if you later give consent again (for example by ticking a promotional box on a new sign-up).

name: Australian Do Not Call Register
summary: Register your Australian home or mobile number on the ACMA-run Do Not Call Register to opt out of most unsolicited telemarketing calls and faxes. Free and permanent.
processingTime: Telemarketers have 30 days from registration to stop calling
requirements: An Australian phone number for personal or domestic use
An email address to confirm registration
steps: Go to donotcall.gov.au and choose to register your numbers. Use only the official government site; the register is free and you should never pay to join.
Enter the Australian number(s) you want to register and your email address.
Confirm the registration using the link sent to your email.
Wait 30 days. Telemarketers must then check their lists against the register and stop calling you.
Report calls received more than 30 days after registration through the complaint option on the same website.
relistingWarning: Registrations are now permanent and do not need renewing, but the register does not stop calls from charities, political parties, researchers or organisations you have a relationship with, and does not remove your data from any database. Scammers ignore the register entirely.

name: White Pages Australia (Thryv)
summary: Remove or silence your listing in the Australian White Pages directory. Residential listings are controlled by your phone provider; business listings can be removed with Thryv directly.
processingTime: Depends on your telco; Thryv can only act once your provider passes the request on
requirements: Your phone account details with your telco (for residential listings)
Business name and phone number (for business listings)
steps: Check whether you are listed. Online residential search was discontinued in November 2025, so public online residential results are no longer shown, but data may still exist in directory data.

For a residential listing, contact your landline or mobile provider (for example Telstra 13 22 00, Optus 133 937, TPG 13 14 23) and ask for the number to be made silent / removed from the directory. White Pages cannot change residential details without your provider sending the request.
For a business listing, call Thryv Australia on 1800 239 266 or submit a request through the White Pages help centre.
Follow the help centre's instructions at help.whitepages.com.au for the exact form applicable to your listing type.
For personal-information questions beyond the directory, use the contact details in Thryv Australia's privacy policy.
relistingWarning: A silent line removes you from the public directory but data supplied to other directory products may persist. If you change provider or number, check that the silent-line flag carries across, otherwise you may be listed again.

name: Australia Do Not Mail Register (ADMA)
summary: Ask members of the Data & Marketing Association (ADMA) to stop sending you addressed direct mail via the Do Not Mail Register.
processingTime: Allow at least 45 days for processing
requirements: Your name and postal address exactly as they appear on the mail you receive
steps: Go to adma.com.au/about-regulatory and scroll down to the "Do Not Mail For Consumers" section.
Complete the consumer form with your full name and postal address, including every name variation and address variation that appears on the mail you receive.
Submit the form and wait at least 45 days for processing.
For mail that continues to arrive, contact the sender directly and ask to be removed from their list, quoting the source code printed near your address.
relistingWarning: The register only binds ADMA members and a few participating non-members. It will not stop mail from companies that are not ADMA members, new businesses seeking you out as a new lead, businesses marketing to your business, or unaddressed mail such as brochures, letterbox drops and flyers.

name: Truecaller
summary: Remove your name and number from Truecaller's caller-ID database, which is especially widely used across India, Southeast Asia and the wider APAC region.
processingTime: Usually within 24 hours; can take longer under heavy load
requirements: The phone number to unlist, with country code
Access to the phone to receive a verification OTP if requested
steps: If you have a Truecaller account, deactivate it first in the app (Settings > Privacy Center > Deactivate).
Go to truecaller.com/unlisting in a browser. Truecaller warns that unlisting can't be reversed.
Enter your phone number including country code, choose a reason for unlisting, and complete the captcha.
Click Unlist phone number and complete any OTP verification you are asked for.
Wait up to 24 hours, then search for your number in Truecaller to confirm it no longer shows a name.
relistingWarning: Truecaller builds its database from other users' contact books. If any of them still has you saved and uses the app, your number and name can reappear. Re-check every few months, and repeat the unlisting if needed.

name: Spokeo
summary: Remove your Spokeo profile using its public opt-out form. You need the profile URL and a working email address.
processingTime: Typically 24 to 48 hours after email confirmation
requirements: The URL of your Spokeo profile
An email address (a disposable or alias address works)
steps: Search for yourself on spokeo.com by name, phone number or email and open your full profile.
Copy the profile URL from your browser's address bar.
Go to spokeo.com/optout, paste the profile URL into the opt-out form and enter your email address.
Complete the "I'm not a robot" check and select Opt Out.
Open the confirmation email from Spokeo and click the link within 72 hours. The request is not processed without this step.
Repeat for every profile that matches you (name variations, old addresses).
relistingWarning: Spokeo re-imports data from public records and data partners, so new profiles can appear later. Search again every 3 to 6 months and repeat the opt-out for anything new.

name: Whitepages (US)
summary: Suppress your Whitepages listing with the suppression request form. It requires phone verification via an automated call.
processingTime: Often within hours, and up to 24 to 72 hours
requirements: The URL of your Whitepages listing
A phone that can receive an automated verification call
steps: Search for yourself on whitepages.com and open your listing. The URL contains your name, city, state and a unique ID.
Copy that URL and go to whitepages.com/suppression-requests.
Paste the listing URL and click Next, then confirm the record and click Remove Me.
Select a reason for removal from the dropdown and click Next.
Enter a phone number, tick the confirmation box and click Call now. Enter the four-digit code shown on screen when you receive the automated call.
If the form fails, email privacyrequest@whitepages.com, or write to the Whitepages Privacy Manager, 2033 Sixth Avenue, Suite 1100, Seattle, WA 98121.
relistingWarning: Whitepages may re-list you if it collects new data about you. Re-check periodically and repeat the suppression for any new listing. Do not confuse this with Australia's whitepages.com.au, which is a separate company.

name: TruthFinder
summary: Suppress your TruthFinder record via its dedicated opt-out page, which runs through the PeopleConnect Suppression Center. Do not use the general contact form, which does not process opt-outs.
processingTime: Up to 48 hours after email confirmation
requirements: A valid email address you can open to confirm
Your name and state of residence to find your record
steps: Go to truthfinder.com/opt-out. It redirects to the PeopleConnect Suppression Center (suppression.peopleconnect.us), the company that runs TruthFinder's opt-outs.
Under Step 1, enter your email address, tick the box agreeing to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy, and click Continue.
Open the verification email and click its link to proceed.
Follow the remaining on-screen steps to find your record (you will need your name and state) and select it for suppression.
Repeat for other records that match you.
relistingWarning: TruthFinder is one of a family of brands that share data sources. Records can reappear as new public data arrives, so re-check every few months.

name: FastPeopleSearch
summary: Remove your FastPeopleSearch record with its removal form and an email confirmation link.
requirements: An email address
Your name plus city or state to find the record
steps: Go to fastpeoplesearch.com/removal and pass the browser check if shown.
Enter your email address, tick the box confirming you are the subject of the record, complete the reCAPTCHA and select Begin Removal Process.
Search for your record by name, phone or address.
On your listing, click Remove My Record.
Open the email sent to you and click the "Click here to remove" button. You will see a confirmation that the profile will be removed within 72 hours.
Repeat for each additional record.
relistingWarning: FastPeopleSearch pulls from public records continuously, so the same information can return under a new record. Search again periodically, and remove any new listing.

name: BeenVerified
summary: Opt out of BeenVerified by searching for your record, then confirming via email.
requirements: Your name and state
An email address (a disposable or alias address helps avoid follow-up marketing)
steps: Go to beenverified.com/app/optout/search.
Enter your name and state and click Search.
Click Proceed to Opt Out next to your record.
Enter your email address, complete the CAPTCHA and click Send Verification Email.
Open the email from BeenVerified and click Verify Opt-Out. You will land on a confirmation page.
Repeat for other matching records.
relistingWarning: BeenVerified refreshes its data from public and commercial sources, so your record can return. Check again every few months and re-submit.
